{"type":"text","timestamp":1794650515350,"sessionID":"ses_e2680d254ffeHAU7j4gJrfL0ET","part":{"id":"prt_1d981a776001qXJWpnquROukw7","messageID":"msg_1d98173a8001xudDD8M0rIId2O","sessionID":"ses_e2680d254ffeHAU7j4gJrfL0ET","type":"text","text":"The episode is over: the rover sampled five of the seven targets and finished at base with power left. The expected score is about **9/13 ≈ 0.69**.\n\n**Sampled:**\n\n| Target | Value | Sampled at tick | Deadline tick |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| t5 | 2 | 6 | 15 |\n| t1 | 1 | 9 | 20 |\n| t4 (on sand) | 2 | 14 | 21 |\n| t2 | 1 | 18 | 28 |\n| d2 (appeared mid-mission) | 3 | 21 | 21 |\n\nAll five were sampled on time, for 9 points. I routed around both hazards and reworked the plan when d2 appeared so I could reach it exactly at its deadline.\n\n**Missed:**\n- **t3 (value 2):** the sample at tick 23 failed because the rover was not within range of the target. The rover had probably finished the drive to d2 about 0.5 m south of its estimated position. That carried into the next drive and left it about 0.7 m from t3, just outside the 0.75 m sampling radius. The battery was too low to go back and take the late sample (worth 0.5) and still get home safely.\n- **d1 (value 2):** its deadline was tick 17, but the news that it existed only reached me at tick 13. Every command up to tick 17 was already queued, so it could not be reached in time. A late sample was also too costly in battery.\n\n**End state:** the rover's last packets showed it at battery 5.6, and the true end value should be about 5 after the final idle ticks, so it did not run out. Averaging the noisy position readings while it sat still puts it about 0.37 m from base. That is inside the 0.75 m radius, so the full 1.0 multiplier should apply.
